title: Indirect questions 2
note: Embedded statement order after tell me / know / wonder. · Bank 8 · order-zone gaps 2026-07-26 · Match off 2026-07-26 · dressed 8→24 items 2026-08-16 (Patrik: "ask him when is he") · 2026-08-19: item 17 duplicated item 2 ('how much it costs') — replaced · 2026-09-04 B1 loop: D1 — two explanations covered 20 of 24 items; each now quotes the direct question it came from and says whether the fault would be do-support or inversion. A2 two items whose Czech named no subject now name one (your brother, your sister). A4 eight Czech prompts gained the demonstrative that licenses their `the`. A8 twin closed on the would-like item. · 2026-09-05 B1 loop: 24 -> 30 items. I7 — the previous run renamed two subjects (he -> your brother / your sister) and left the old strings in `gap_accepts` and in `wrong`; since `wrong` is the Use prompt, a student who correctly repaired *where does he work* was graded against *your brother works* and marked wrong. Both closed. B8 — item 12 still hid `if` inside the gap, which is the exact flag from the 2026-08-30 smoke ('question should have if in it'); `if` is now on the stem. E9 — item 18 (*who is responsible*) had no `wrong`, and a subject-*who* question has no inversion to undo, so it is `use: false` rather than carrying an invented error. Intro 8 -> 6 cards: C20 cut the Practice focus card (it described the drill, not the language); C32/C27 merged the two one-row CZ trap cards into one Common mistakes table with `~~strike~~` rows, so the errors look like errors instead of carrying a ✗; the Form card stopped restating card 1's own row and now shows the three slots. The six new items add the modal-inversion error (*where can I buy*), which is now a row on that card, and three more past-tense *did* items — the bank had only three. The 3 F3 CANDIDATEs are the *wonder* items and stand: lint's `taught` set is prior-path packs plus this pack's own gap_answers, and *wonder* is a frame verb that never lands in a gap.

items.en: Can you tell me where the station is?
items.cz: Můžeš mi říct, kde je to nádraží?
items.gap: Can you tell me where ____? (station / be)
accepts: Can you tell me where the station is?
items.explanation: **the station is** is statement order — subject, then verb. *is the station* is direct-question order, which an indirect question never takes. Can you tell me where the station is?
items.explanation_cz: **the station is** je pořádek oznamovací věty — podmět, pak sloveso. *is the station* je pořádek přímé otázky, který nepřímá otázka nikdy nemá. Can you tell me where the station is?
items.wrong: Can you tell me where is the station?

items.en: Do you know what time the train leaves?

accepts: Do you know what time the train leaves?
Do you know what time the train will leave?
items.explanation: The direct question is *does the train leave?* — inside this sentence the **does** disappears and the verb carries the tense: **the train leaves**. Do you know what time the train leaves?
items.explanation_cz: Přímá otázka zní *does the train leave?* — uvnitř této věty **does** mizí a čas nese sloveso: **the train leaves**. Do you know what time the train leaves?
items.wrong: Do you know what time does the train leave?

cards.title: Direct questions
points: Question form: the helper (**do** / **be**) before the subject.

cards.title: Indirect questions
points: Still questions. They do **not** use question form.
After the frame: subject + verb (no helper).

rows: Can you tell me where the station **is**?
Can you tell me where he **works**?
Do you know if the shop **is** open?

cards.title: Form
points: Three slots, always in this order.
Nothing changes shape in the third slot.

cards.title: do / does / did disappear

rows: Do you know where he lives?

points: The verb takes its normal ending

cards.title: Yes–no questions → if / whether

rows: Do you know if it is open?

points: Yes/no → if or whether + statement order

cards.title: Common mistakes

rows: ~~Can you tell me where is the station?~~
Can you tell me where the station **is**?
~~Can you tell me what time does the train leave?~~
Can you tell me what time the train **leaves**?
~~Can you tell me where can I buy a ticket?~~
Can you tell me where **I can** buy a ticket?

points: Czech keeps question order inside; English does not.
The helper **do**, **does** or **did** never survives the move.
